diverge.why: V8 exposes no per-iteration allocation count. Node offers heap totals through process.memoryUsage and v8.getHeapStatistics, and neither counts allocations, so there is no number to hold to a ceiling.
diverge.remedy: A counter in V8's API, or a profiler sampling allocations, which is too slow to run per iteration.

diverge.why: V8 exposes no allocation count, for the reason the bench-max-allocs entry gives, so there is no count per call to hold to a ceiling.
diverge.remedy: The counter in V8's API that bench-max-allocs needs.

diverge.why: The form runs max-allocs on each input, and max-allocs is absent for the reason its entry gives.
diverge.remedy: The counter in V8's API that bench-max-allocs needs.

diverge.why: Node releases the backing store of a freed typed array on a background thread after the collection. On Node 26.12.1 a freed array of 256 KiB stayed in process.memoryUsage().arrayBuffers after gc(), after a second gc(), after a last-resort collection, after a microtask, after setImmediate and after setTimeout(0), and left it about 10 ms later. A synchronous probe therefore reads freed buffers as kept, and heapUsed alone does not count the backing stores at all, so no reading can hold a call to a ceiling.
diverge.remedy: A collection in V8 or Node that releases the backing stores of freed array buffers before it returns.

diverge.why: V8 exposes no allocation count, for the reason the bench-max-allocs entry gives, so there is no count per call to hold to a ceiling, with a setup or without one.
diverge.remedy: The counter in V8's API that bench-max-allocs needs.

diverge.why: The form runs max-allocs-with-setup on each input, and max-allocs-with-setup is absent for the reason its entry gives.
diverge.remedy: The counter in V8's API that bench-max-allocs needs.

diverge.why: Bytes allocated per iteration can only be read as a heap-usage delta, which moves with whether the collector ran. Measuring one unchanged body six times gave 43, -3, 43, -10, -10 and -8 bytes per iteration, so a ceiling set from one run fails the next for no reason.
diverge.remedy: A per-iteration allocation total that does not depend on collector timing.

limits.what: Carries no lock. The runtime has one thread, so two assertions cannot report at the same instant.
limits.why: The standard asks that a seat be usable from more than one thread. A runtime with one thread meets that without doing anything, and says so here rather than leaving a reader to work out which it is.

limits.what: Runs one case at a time, whatever the number of workers. The run reports what a run on one worker reports, as it does in every language.
limits.why: A body runs on the runtime's one thread. An asynchronous body would interleave with another case at each await instead of running beside it, and a body that is not safe to interleave with itself would then fail in a way that a run on one worker never shows.

limits.what: Does not run a fuzzer under vitest. Under vitest, prop.fuzz replays the cases that the store keeps for the property, as Go's prop.Fuzz does under go test without -fuzz. It returns the target that a fuzzer runs on its byte inputs, such as Jazzer.js.
limits.why: vitest has no fuzzing mode, and Node has no fuzzer in its standard library. The library depends on no fuzzer, so a suite that fuzzes exports the target to a fuzzer that it installs itself.

limits.what: Gives a property form the generator of its input. A run of forAll and fuzz and a call of prop.values do not take the option, because the body or the caller states each generator that it draws from.
limits.why: The TypeScript compiler erases every type, so a run has no type to give a generator to. A property derives its inputs from shape files alone, and a form takes its input's generator through using.

limits.what: Searches one partition at a time, whatever the number of workers. A check reports what a check on one worker reports, as it does in every language.
limits.why: A spec is a set of functions, and the structured clone that copies a message to a worker thread refuses a function, so every partition is searched on the runtime's one thread.

limits.what: Skips the test through the seat of the vitest fixture test, which calls skip of the test context. On every other seat, the seat of a jest test included, the call record states the verdict skip and the test passes.
limits.why: jest offers no call that skips a test while it runs, and a seat outside the fixture has no test context to call skip on.

limits.what: Only the seat of the vitest fixture test states the member, which calls skip of the test context. A call of doesReject whose check skips on any other seat, the seat of a jest test included, states the verdict skip in its call record, and the test passes.
limits.why: jest offers no call that skips a test while it runs, and a seat outside the fixture has no test context to call skip on.

surface.why: The seat states report and clock itself, with a default, so a seat that supplies neither gets the platform clock and a rendered sentence. Only a language whose interfaces carry no defaults needs a second interface to say the same thing.

The seat states reportFault as an optional member, which the library calls where the seat has it, and the library throws the fault for a seat without it. Only a language whose interfaces carry no defaults needs a second interface to say the same thing.

The harness owns the loop here, so setup goes in a second closure, handed to measuring, that the harness runs outside the measurement. Marking the setup in place would need the body to reach the contract it was handed to.
JavaScript runs every worker on one thread. Workers would interleave only where the body awaits, so a parallel body would measure the queue of the event loop and not contention between threads.
repeat sets the number of runs of a case whose concurrent section runs on real threads. A section runs here only as tasks of the task scheduler, which replays it from the case.

records.artifact: The JSON report that vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile.json=PATH writes to PATH when the run ends. Vitest's JUnit report states test annotations and no task meta, and an annotation cannot be written after a test's function returns.
records.location: The array under the key of the record's kind, such as dokimi.assert or dokimi.suite, of the meta object of the test's entry in testResults[].assertionResults[], one record per element, in the order the records are made. The entry's ancestorTitles and title name the test inside the file that testResults[].name names.
records.status: The status field of the same entry: passed, failed, skipped, todo or pending.
